title: The normalized smooth trace represents compact-support morphisms uniquely
statement: For a prime ell, a positive-characteristic field k with ell invertible, separated finite-type k-schemes X and Y, a morphism f smooth of pure relative dimension d, a bounded constructible coefficient object M on X identified with the shifted Tate twist, and the tensor unit U on Y, there exists a unique morphism t : Rf_! M -> U such that postcomposition with t gives a bijection Hom(K,M) -> Hom(Rf_! K,U) for every bounded constructible K. This is the normalized finite-diagonal and adic-reconstruction representing-pair step used to construct smoothTrace.

source.place: def-route-smooth-trace, Steps 1--4: finite smooth-purity adjunction, normalized adic reconstruction, and condensed realization of the representing counit

proof.text: Completed finite/input step: smoothTrace_nativeSystem supplies the normalized positive finite orientations, the actual finite representing trace Hom bijections and their quotient-counit equations, together with ReconstructionResult for the same native compactification. The private smoothTrace_nativeReconstructionInputs applies this to the exact Over-morphism hypotheses of the item. This does not yet construct a condensed trace.

Remaining geometric construction: transport the actual normalized finite Hom pairing through integral reconstruction, rationalization and condensed scalar extension, using the normalized Tate and unit comparisons. The input reconstruction package is available, but the actual natural condensed Hom equivalence and its normalization are not constructed in this module.

STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the displayed conclusion asks for uniqueness among all representing traces, omitting the fixed normalized Hom equivalence. The proved classification identifies all representing traces with source automorphisms; unnormalized uniqueness would force every such automorphism to be identity. The existing private closed counterexample at ell=2 over the algebraic closure of F_3 refutes that conclusion. The new normalized-pairing and specified-orientation theorems prove the valid final uniqueness step, but cannot prove this unchanged false statement. No proof or hole closure is claimed.

proof_origin.place: B4 partial proof: finite representing pairings, actual quotient counits and native normalized integral inputs are proved. The last unnormalized uniqueness assertion remains false and admitted; the valid counit-normalized categorical final step is proved separately.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_smoothTrace (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] {k : Type u} [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)] {X Y : Over (Spec (.of k))} [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [IsSeparated X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] [IsSeparated Y.hom] (f : X ⟶ Y) (d : ℕ) (hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f.left) (M : Dᵇc(X.left)⟦Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ⟧) (hM : M.obj ≅ (shiftFunctor _ (2 * d : ℤ)).obj (tateTwistDerived X.left ℓ d)) (U : Dᵇc(Y.left)⟦Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ⟧) (hU : U = MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit (Dᵇc(Y.left)⟦Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ⟧)) : ∃! t : (boundedConstructibleLowerShriek (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) ℓ f).obj M ⟶ U, ∀ K : Dᵇc(X.left)⟦Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ⟧, Function.Bijective (fun a : K ⟶ M ↦ (boundedConstructibleLowerShriek (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) ℓ f).map a ≫ t)
